title: Move sign-in/account-picker test cleanup into addTearDown so a failed assertion doesn't leak the ProviderContainer/Drift DB
why: Both files call their cleanup helper (_tearDown / _tearDownContainer + registry.close()) as the last statement inside each test body, after several `expect()` calls. If any expect() throws (the exact moment a real regression would be caught), cleanup is skipped and the in-memory Drift registry/userDb connections and ProviderContainer leak for the rest of the suite run — the opposite of TQ-2's 'never share state between tests' guarantee, and the failure that most needs a clean teardown is the one that gets skipped. Sibling files in this exact batch (account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart's tearDown(), and the notifier tests' addTearDown(container.dispose)) show the correct, already-established pattern.
recommendation: Replace the manual end-of-test _tearDown/_tearDownContainer calls with addTearDown(...) registered immediately after the container/registry/userDb are created, matching account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart's tearDown() in this same batch.
acceptance_criteria: Cleanup (container dispose, registry.close(), userDb.close()) is registered via addTearDown/tearDown() immediately after creation, not as the final statement of the test body.
A deliberately-failing expect() inserted mid-test still leaves the Drift databases closed.
